subject: Physics
concept: Displacement is the straight-line change in position from start to finish, with direction. Distance is the total path travelled and is always positive — displacement can be zero or negative.

formulas.when_to_use: Any straight-line motion when start and end positions are known.
formulas.derivation: Final minus initial position, keeping the sign for direction.

formulas.when_to_use: Rate of travel along the path, ignoring direction.
formulas.derivation: Total path length divided by total time.

examples.text: Walk from x₀ = 2 m to x = 17 m: displacement Δx = 15 m.
A 400 m lap brings you back to the start: distance 400 m, but displacement 0 m.

practice.prompt: x₀ = 2 m, x = 17 m. Find the displacement Δx.
Distance d = 250 m in time t = 50 s. Find the average speed.
x₀ = 4 m, x = 30 m. Find the displacement Δx.
Distance d = 960 m in time t = 240 s. Find the average speed.
x₀ = 100 m, x = 35 m. Find the displacement Δx (keep the sign).
